significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds for all n ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1. Here α(n; k₁, …, kₙ) is the polynomial that counts monotone triangles with bottom row k₁ < … < kₙ, evaluated at a row with one descent. The proof finds a specific identity among four evaluations of α at neighbouring rows (the four-position identity W1) and certifies it with Fischer's operator formula, by the method of Fischer–Riegler's Lemmas 8.1–8.2; it turns each successive difference in i into a value of α at a row with a repeated entry, which equals the total number A_n of alternating sign matrices, and telescoping from Riegler's published case i = 1 gives the formula. Lean defines α by Fischer's operator formula, proves that it counts monotone triangles at strictly increasing rows, and proves the identity over the full printed range, with A_{n,j} given as α at the deletion rows (and, in a second endpoint, as monotone-triangle counts).
significance.caveat: Lean proves the statement with α defined by Fischer's operator formula; that this α counts monotone triangles at increasing rows is proved in Lean, while two standard identifications are on paper only: polynomiality and uniqueness (so that the operator formula is Riegler's polynomial also at the descent row), and the classical bijection between monotone triangles and alternating sign matrices behind A_{n,j}. The method (operator-formula certificates) is Fischer–Riegler's; the contribution is the specific four-position identity. Riegler's 2014 dissertation still states the conjecture as open (p. 75; read through the text in the catalogue record); one citing thesis (Izanloo 2019) is unread (tangential by its abstract). Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (two rounds; not routine 0.59, close to the floor of 0.55 root uses for counting).
